groups.text: It is currently cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 22 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Open source developers are pushing for tighter hardware integration to squeeze more speed out of large language models. The vLLM project has released version 0.28.0, a massive update featuring 584 commits from 270 contributors. This release focuses heavily on the Kimi-K3 model, introducing optimizations like Decode Context Parallel support and fused FlashKDA kernels to improve performance across the stack. Kimi-K3 can now also run on ROCm using the V2 model runner. Meanwhile, vLLM has added end-to-end sparse MLA support for DeepSeek V4 and enabled ROCm on gfx11 and gfx950. In a separate effort toward local efficiency, llama.cpp released build b10632. This update targets Apple hardware specifically, adding chunked SSD MMA to optimize prefill for Mamba-2 via ggml-metal. While vLLM focuses on scaling infrastructure for massive models like DeepSeek and Kimi, the llama.cpp update prioritizes refining how specific model architectures perform on local Metal-enabled devices.

Hungary has officially described Russia as a threat to Europe and the global order. This language appears in guidelines for the Hungarian delegation attending next month's UN General Assembly. The document condemns Russian military aggression and pledges full support for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its recognized borders. This represents a dramatic shift from the era of Viktor Orban, who was widely seen as one of Europe's most Russia-friendly leaders before Prime Minister Peter Magyar defeated him in elections earlier this year. Budapest and Kyiv have also taken conciliatory steps toward each other recently. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha praised Hungary for closing a money laundering investigation into a Ukrainian bank convoy that had been seized in March while transporting cash and gold from Austria. Sybiha noted that using anti-Ukrainian rhetoric for domestic political gain results only in shame and defeat.

Flash floods have devastated remote valleys in Nepal and Tibet, washing away entire villages, bridges, and electrical infrastructure. In Nepal's Rasuwa district, eight people are confirmed dead, while Chinese authorities report major casualties from a mudslide across the border. Rescue helicopters have struggled to land because floodwaters remain too high. At least 26 Nepali police personnel are missing, along with hydropower workers and government revenue officials. Meanwhile, in Europe, investigators are probing one of Belgium's largest fires in history within the High Fens nature reserve. Three thousand hectares of protected land were destroyed. The Belgian prosecutor is investigating negligent arson, suggesting a piece of agricultural equipment may have sparked the blaze. EU Crisis Commissioner Hadja Lahbib stated the fire was one hundred percent human-caused, likely due to unintentional behavior. In Ukraine, representatives from "We are Ukraine" and the Ministry for Community and Territorial Development are seeking membership on the National Council under the presidential quota.

In Uttar Pradesh’s Banda district, farmers are facing severe water shortages as rainfall remains twenty-six percent below normal for the monsoon season. Vipin Kumar Yadav, a farmer from Manipur village, reports that his ten-foot-deep farm pond failed to reach even five feet this year, whereas it was full last year. This lack of stored water threatens upcoming wheat and mustard crops in a region heavily dependent on rain, especially as the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences warns that El Niño has intensified from weak to moderate levels. Meanwhile, in the tech sector, Anthropic is merging the memory systems of its chatbot, Claude, and its task automation tool, Cowork. By default, both tools can now automatically record and reuse information across platforms. This shared memory allows Cowork to access past chat discussions to adapt its responses or draft reports based on a user's known preferences without needing repeated instructions.

Anthropic is preparing for an initial public offering in September or October while chasing a valuation of about 2 trillion dollars. To attract investors, the company expects to claim a theoretical total addressable market worth more than 30 trillion dollars. This figure represents the annual revenue Anthropic could reach if it owned one hundred percent of all work AI models could take on. That estimate would surpass SpaceX, which claimed a 28.5 trillion dollar market in May. However, these numbers draw doubt when compared to actual earnings. FactSet reports that 191 tech firms in the S&P 1500 pulled in a combined 2.4 trillion dollars last year. Despite this gap, Anthropic doubled its second-quarter revenue to 11.6 billion dollars and expects annual revenue to reach roughly 200 billion dollars by 2028. The company now wants to raise up to 100 billion dollars.

Security challenges are mounting in the remote Kenyan village of Cheporor. A recent discovery of gold has drawn thousands of amateur prospectors to the area over the last few weeks, transforming the village into a bustling small town. However, the location lacks the infrastructure needed to house these new arrivals. In separate news, Google released Chrome 152 on Tuesday to patch more than 300 vulnerabilities. Ten of these flaws received a critical severity rating, while sixty-one were rated as high severity. Google used AI to discover the majority of these weaknesses internally, though external researchers continue to find high-value flaws. One researcher, named Goodluck, earned a twenty-five thousand dollar bug bounty for a critical vulnerability. While Google has patched over two thousand Chrome vulnerabilities so far this year, the company's latest advisory does not mention any exploitation of these specific holes in the wild.

Piero Cipollone of the European Central Bank is pushing to move Europe from a vision to the actual delivery of a tokenised financial market. Speaking at a Deutsche Bundesbank symposium in Frankfurt, Cipollone argued that representing assets as programmable data files can make finance more efficient by allowing automation and around-the-clock operations with fewer intermediaries. He described this shift toward distributed ledger technology as a Copernican revolution for the digital finance ecosystem. However, he warned that if Europe allows too many incompatible platforms to emerge, it could deepen the existing fragmentation of European capital markets. To prevent this, Cipollone is advocating for an integrated ecosystem for digital assets that places central bank money at its core. He noted that while these goals remain the cardinal points for the ECB, the focus has now shifted toward the practical steps of implementation.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be clear with temperatures between 21 and 26 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has Antje's birthday. Your work calendar has Optikrunde at ten in the morning and a group meeting with Gregor at three in the afternoon.
Mail worth checking: Kleinanzeigen sent new search results for a pro gauntlet.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
